cards.title: Whose poster is it?
cards.body:
In a town poster competition, one entrant types a prompt and gets an amazing poster in seconds. Another spends a week painting theirs.

Using AI is often fine. Hiding it usually isn't. **Say how you used it**, **follow the rules** (and ask when you're not sure), and **don't claim AI's work as yours**.

items.label: "I used AI to check my spelling"
Asking first if AI is allowed
Using AI ideas, writing it, saying so
Entering an AI picture as your own art
Giving an AI-written speech as yours
Saying "no" when asked if you used AI

cards.hint: Look for whether the person is open about the AI's part.
cards.nudge: Using AI isn't the problem. Which ones hide it, or claim its work?
cards.explanation: Saying how you used AI, asking first and writing it yourself are **honest**. Entering AI art as yours, giving an AI speech as yours, or denying it when asked are **not**, however good the result.

cards.prompt: Your teacher says no AI for an essay. You want to use AI just to fix your spelling. What should you do?

options.text: Use a different AI app, so it isn't the one that's banned
options.nudge: The rule is about AI, not one app. What would make it clear?

options.text: Just use it: fixing spelling doesn't really count
options.nudge: It might be fine, but it isn't your call when the rule says no AI. Who decides?

options.text: Ask your teacher whether AI spelling help counts
Use it, and tell your teacher after you hand it in
options.nudge: Saying so is good, but the rule was set before. What should you do first?

cards.hint: When you're not sure if something breaks a rule, who should you ask?
cards.explanation: When you're not sure, **ask first**. Spelling help might be allowed, but it's your teacher's rule to explain, not yours to guess.

cards.prompt:
AI learned from huge amounts of work by people: artists' pictures, writers' stories, musicians' songs. Many weren't asked, and people still disagree about what's fair.

You love one illustrator's style, and use AI to make a poster in that style for your band's gig. What's the **fairest** thing to do?

options.text: Credit the illustrator who inspired it, and say AI helped make it
Say nothing: a style can't belong to anyone, so no credit is needed
options.nudge: People argue about styles, but this one came from a real person's work. Is hiding that fair to them, or to your audience?

options.text: Say nothing, as long as the AI app you used was free
options.nudge: The price of the app doesn't change whose work it learned from. What would be fair to the artist?

options.text: Say you drew it yourself, since choosing the style was your idea
options.nudge: Choosing a style is your idea, but the drawing isn't your work. Look back at what's honest.

cards.hint: Two things are true here: a real artist inspired it, and AI made it. Which answer is open about both?
cards.explanation: **Credit the artist and say AI helped.** That respects the person whose work inspired it, and it's honest with everyone who sees the poster. Your own ideas and voice are still yours.

cards.prompt:
Remember [[bias]]: AI can work better for some people than others. When AI picks, sorts or scores people, it's worth asking who it might leave out, and keeping a person in charge of decisions that matter.

Your sports club wants an AI tool to pick team captains "fairly", based on who talks most at training.

steps.text: What's the best thing to say?

choices.text: "It's fair: everyone is judged by the same rule"
choices.consequence: The same rule for everyone can still be unfair, if the rule itself leaves people out. Quiet players would never get picked.

choices.text: "Who might this be unfair to? Quiet players can lead too"
choices.consequence: Exactly. Talking a lot isn't the same as leading well. The club agrees to have a person decide, using more than one thing.

choices.text: "Fine, as long as it also counts who scores the most goals"
choices.consequence: Another number doesn't ask who the rule leaves out, and the AI is still deciding alone. Quiet players who'd lead well still miss out.

cards.hint: Look back at the question to ask whenever AI makes decisions about people.
cards.explanation: Judging by who **talks most** leaves out quieter people who could lead well, even though it's the same rule for everyone, and adding another number doesn't fix that. Ask **who it might be unfair to**, and keep a **person** deciding.

cards.prompt: Match each situation to the fair thing to do.

pairs.left: An AI picture for an art contest
pairs.right: Say it's AI, or don't enter it

pairs.left: AI helped you plan an essay
Your art copies an artist's style

cards.hint: Each fix is about being open, or about keeping people in charge.
cards.nudge: One is about credit for someone else's work, one about decisions about people, and two about saying what the AI did.
cards.explanation: Be **open** about AI pictures and essay help, **credit** artists who inspire you, and keep **a person deciding** when AI picks people.

cards.prompt: Your friend's story wins a writing prize. You know a chatbot wrote most of it.

steps.text: The competition rules said "your own work only". What's the fairest thing to do?

choices.text: Tell the other entrants, since it's unfair on them
choices.consequence: It is unfair on them, but this could embarrass your friend in front of everyone before they've had a chance to put it right.

choices.text: Talk to your friend privately, and encourage them to tell the organisers
choices.consequence: Fair to your friend and to the others who entered. If they won't, you can talk to a trusted adult about it.

choices.text: Say nothing: it's the judges' job to spot AI writing
choices.consequence: Judges can't always tell, and the rules said own work only. Other people did theirs themselves, so staying quiet isn't fair on them.

cards.hint: Think about being fair to the other entrants, and kind to your friend.
cards.explanation: Talking to your friend **privately** gives them the chance to put it right, which is fair to everyone who did their own work. A trusted adult can help if they won't.

cards.title: You know how AI really works
cards.body:
- AI learns **patterns from examples**: only as good, and fair, as its data.
- Chatbots pick **likely words**, not checked facts: check what matters.
- Fakes are cheap: check **outside** the post, and use AI **openly**.

Next: the course final.
